cases.intent: Plan and sequence a new campus that needs addressing, hardware, security, services, voice, redundancy, dynamic routing, deployment, and validation.
Coordinate the phased migration of an enterprise topology across design, capacity, configuration, domain services, and acceptance.
Break a multi-domain branch rollout into owned work steps and define the handoffs between them.
Define the logical site hierarchy, trust zones, and resilience objectives for a new campus.
Translate business connectivity requirements into a logical enterprise topology before assigning addresses or device models.
Review whether a proposed campus hierarchy and redundancy intent form a coherent logical design.
Allocate growth-aware IPv4 subnets and reservations for the floors and shared services.
Reconcile deployed IPv4 identities with a revised addressing plan while preserving valid assignments.
Calculate access ports, PoE demand, uplinks, and growth headroom before choosing hardware.
Select switch and router models that satisfy an approved port, PoE, uplink, and redundancy demand.
Choose modules and interfaces for a hardware plan using the currently established capability evidence.
Evaluate candidate device selections against the approved physical capacity requirements.
Arrange the existing campus devices into a readable hierarchical layout without changing connectivity.
Reposition already-defined devices deterministically while preserving topology semantics.
Improve the visual placement of a deployed topology without adding tiers, links, or policies.
Compile and apply an already-approved foundational configuration plan through typed actions.
Apply approved interface, VLAN, trunk, and addressing mechanics without redesigning domain policy.
Inspect why a typed foundational configuration action failed to apply or read back.
Correct an approved access-port configuration through the existing typed configuration workflow.
Define and verify DNS and NTP behavior for the enterprise services plan.
Configure the approved HTTP, HTTPS, and TFTP service intent and collect service-specific evidence.
Check whether enterprise clients can use the declared infrastructure services without testing phone calls.
Provision the approved voice workflow and verify that phones register with call control.
Collect evidence for an end-to-end call between registered enterprise phones.
Investigate a failed phone registration using the voice plan and current voice observations.
Define and verify an ACL policy with both permitted and denied traffic evidence.
Apply an approved NAT policy and evaluate its security-specific translation evidence.
Assess port-security or other layer-two enforcement for a specific security control.
Choose and verify the spanning-tree root and recovery behavior for the campus access layer.
Validate EtherChannel membership, bundle state, and failover without changing ordinary trunk plumbing.
Investigate a campus layer-two resilience failure using current STP and EtherChannel evidence.
Define the redundant default-gateway virtual IP and verify gateway role behavior.
Test first-hop gateway failover and recovery for hosts that use the virtual gateway.
Inspect current FHRP role and forwarding evidence without evaluating route exchange.
Configure typed RIPv2 intent and verify learned routes and forwarding behavior.
Evaluate OSPFv2 adjacency and routing evidence for an approved control-plane design.
Investigate EIGRP route exchange while preserving UNKNOWN or UNOBSERVABLE evidence where current probes cannot decide.
Determine whether the current Packet Tracer environment supports the device feature needed by a proposed plan.
Run an isolated capability probe and interpret UNKNOWN without treating it as unsupported.
Resolve current protocol support from governed capability evidence before selecting an operational path.
Deploy an approved topology into Packet Tracer and confirm fresh read-back before continuing.
Operate the controlled live lifecycle through readiness, convergence, observation, and cleanup.
Query current device state and verify the observation is fresh without deciding domain policy.
Evaluate whether the completed deployment satisfies its declared expectations using fresh governed evidence.
Produce an acceptance verdict for the approved scenario without inferring that completion alone means verification.
Check whether readiness, forwarding, services, security, and recovery evidence meet the deployment intent.
Explain why a previously accepted connectivity expectation is now failing using the first evidence-supported causal invariant.
Trace a packet failure and identify the earliest supported cause without changing the topology.
Investigate a failed validation result with current observations while preserving unknown evidence states.
Run the current pt_fix_plan helper on a TopologyPlan with an invalid cable type or insufficient router ports.
Automatically diagnose and repair whatever is wrong in the live network, then roll back if the repair fails.
